_about: The righteousness hub (plan 7.6f), the second built to prove the design transfers: love leads with the verb, righteousness with the noun. Rows as in love.json; 'in_verse' is a word anywhere in the verse ("do righteousness": the verb stands outside the noun's phrase). The committee flagged it high (2026-10-09): 'the righteousness of God' kept as written, with no gloss on whose; 'by faith' and 'by works' side by side. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py.
_shown_why: Doug, 2026-10-09: 'approve of the contents of both'
_words_why: Doug, 2026-10-09: 'if righteous is the adjective form of the same word, it does not need the same treatment' (as love's other words). Measured: every word the text renders righteous/righteousness is of the צדק or δικ- family but for single stray glosses, so there is no 'other words' section; δικαίωμα (10) and δικαίωσις (2, Rom 4:25, 5:18) are the family's and were missing. δικαίως (5) is an adverb, which the forms do not take.

Acts.13.38.why: the Greek's 13:38 ends 'from all which you could not be justified by the law of Moses'; the Berean prints those words in 13:39, so 13:38 as shown has no 'justified'

_review: Nine-reader review, 2026-10-09 (ontology/provenance/concept-hubs/righteousness-review.json): 'ship after fixes', 12 of 18 rows. Taken as rules: a verse sits in every row it fits (match: all), so the order no longer decides Jas 2:24 or Rom 1:17; 'of God' as a phrase (adjacent), not God anywhere in the clause (Deut 9:4, 1 John 3:10); seek and do by the grammar's object (object_of), so 'persecuted because of righteousness' (Matt 5:10, διώκω) is its own row; faith and works in the verb's own clause (1 Tim 3:16 is a hymn's next line); the Greek 'judgment' apart from the Hebrew 'justice'; labels that name every companion word; 'credited' as the text's own phrase; who is called righteous split as the text names them, Jesus by hand. Second review (righteousness-review-2.json): most resolved, 10 new; taken as: in_verse read from the verse's own words (not clauses that start in it), the phrase window to the very next word, 'lead' for examples that show the label, 'add' for the LORD's righteousness addressed in the second person, persecuted by hand.
